body:
SUPERSEDED, now "never" (Termal::Fable2, 2026-10-16 22:08Z). Greg REVOKED the auto-approve direction (Engram::Advisor, TermAl mailbox b9d13887 #922, 22:07:38Z), verbatim: "Greg revokes the prior auto-approve direction. Immediately set approvalPolicy `never` through the supported settings route for all eight sessions previously changed: 7899, 9860, 11312, 11323, 11330, 11334, 8581, 7305. For future coding/implementation sessions, use `never`, not auto-approve. Read back and report effective policy per session. Do not answer any pending elicitation or ordinary approval automatically; Greg handles prompts explicitly. This supersedes the earlier auto-approve messages." APPLIED 22:08Z: all 8 now read back "never".

RULE: new coding sessions use approvalPolicy "never" (POST /api/sessions {"agent": "Codex", "approvalPolicy": "never"}). NEVER use "auto-approve" for MCP-using agents. TermAl's AutoApprove maps to Codex "on-request" (src/wire.rs:865), which makes Codex ask before every MCP tool call, as an elicitation that auto-approve doesn't answer, so the session PARKS on its first mailbox or tracker call. My 21:56Z switch caused 7899 and 8581 to park at 22:06Z. The lesson: check the mapping to the runtime's actual flag before applying any approval-policy change.

History: Advisor #916 asked for auto-approve on new sessions; #918 authorized switching 8 existing sessions, which I applied at 21:56Z; #922 revoked both.

22:13Z, Greg's clarified architecture (Advisor #930; #928's option 3 withdrawn). Codex "never" is the Codex-side setting; TermAl auto-approve is a HOST policy and must not be passed to Codex as on-request. P0 w-fa936228028f fixes the mapping (owner Termal::Coder); its criteria are in the 22:13Z note on the item. Until it lands, "never" stays as containment everywhere, and no session goes back to auto-approve without Greg's word.
